newPrimaryFindings.finding: Official court identifies the Sixth Judicial District as Grant, Hidalgo and Luna counties. This corroborates the geographic limitation; it does not make every lower court in those counties a District Court.

Official local page permits free process or fee reduction upon indigency by court order and points to the local General Forms. Its civil-case schedule is not a finding that every assigned expungement route has an identical charge. Current local payment methods include counter cards, so a general old cash/check-only rule must not be repeated for this venue.

Official forms catalogue supplies local form discovery, not proof that this held historical binary is the latest downloadable edition. No exact current replacement file is claimed from a catalogue link.

scopeDecision.remainingLocalCurrencyQuestion: The physical source is demonstrably Sixth District. Whether that district currently accepts this exact historical edition for a selected case has not been established by a new issuer-byte comparison or clerk response. No acceptance is invented.

commonImplementationAnswer.instrument: When the actual fee-relief branch is selected, the appropriate local or statewide Application for Free Process and Affidavit of Indigency under Rule23-114. The held composite supplies five-page4-222 and a separate two-page4-223 judicial order, restricted to its own District Court caption.
commonImplementationAnswer.actor: Applicant supplies genuine financial facts and executes the source's oath; notary executes jurat. Attorney certificate is conditional on actual representation. Judge makes indigency findings, selects costs/service relief, signs and enters4-223. No judge choices or financial zeros are participant prefills.
commonImplementationAnswer.destination: Clerk of the district court for the venue selected by the underlying expungement route. Only an actual Sixth District venue can match the held static caption; participant residence alone does not choose the expungement court.
commonImplementationAnswer.trigger: Actual inability to pay and request for fee relief under the existing conditional component. Sponsorship and absence of payment data are not indigency or waiver approval.
commonImplementationAnswer.timing: Application asks relief from prepayment. Do not demand an already-signed judicial order as a participant prerequisite or infer that submitting the request automatically extends another filing/service/hearing deadline. No independent deadline for this application was established by this scope review.
commonImplementationAnswer.components: Keep4-222 and4-223 distinct even when delivered in one PDF. Do not duplicate4-223 if the existing selected packet already includes those last two pages. Maintain actual representation and execution conditions.
commonImplementationAnswer.feesWaiver: Free process is ordered, not self-certified as granted. Source4-223 says several ancillary costs are excluded unless expressly granted; do not convert it to a blanket waiver. The current local civil-fee schedule does not settle the retained identity-theft-specific fee question. No new statewide fee amount is supplied.
commonImplementationAnswer.noticeService: Do not import4-223's conditional sheriff-service relief as the service procedure for every expungement petition. Preserve the separate underlying-route service rules. Judicial service relief and completed-service certificates remain real future acts.
commonImplementationAnswer.selfHelpBoundary: Stop this source's use when venue is unknown, outside Sixth District, the court type differs, the required financial/representation facts are missing, or the actual order conflicts with requested relief. Preserve existing contested-matter and conviction-family self-help stops; no new professional approval requirement is manufactured.
